blocks.text: David Dyer, General Manager, Johnson PLC
Dear Mr. Dyer:

This letter sets out the terms on which this office will prepare a stormwater management plan for {{fact:f:E-2004-001.client}}. When you have read it and returned a signed copy, it will serve as our agreement for the work. The terms below govern how we will proceed, what we will deliver, and what each of us is responsible for.
The Work

We will prepare a complete stormwater management plan for the site. The plan will address the drainage of the developed property, the detention of stormwater to control the rate of runoff, and the treatment of that runoff for water quality. It will be prepared to the standards of the regional water authority that reviews such plans in this jurisdiction. Our drawings will be issued under a sealed cover sheet, and the calculations that support them will be included in the submission.

The work proceeds in the order the design requires. We begin with the survey and topographic data for the site and the drainage areas they define. We build the hydrologic and hydraulic model from that base and establish the flows the plan must manage. We then size the detention and water quality facilities to meet the required release rates and prepare the erosion and sediment control plan that accompanies the design. When the design is set, we assemble the plan set and the supporting calculations for submission and for the reviewing agency's examination. Our fee includes one round of response to that agency's written comments.
Assignments

Pamela Warren, Project Engineer, will lead the design and carry the coordination with the regional water authority's reviewers. Charles Olson and Jeffrey Perez, Design Technicians, will prepare the plan sheets and the utility and stormwater drafting from her direction. I will review every sheet and seal the completed set. Any correspondence to the reviewing agency or to another public body will be issued over my signature. You may direct questions on the day-to-day work to Pamela Warren, and questions on scope, fee, or the terms of this agreement to me.
Information and Reliance

Our design will rely on the accuracy of the survey, the boundary information, and the site plan furnished to us or prepared under separate agreement. We will review that information for consistency, but we are entitled to rely on it and are not responsible for errors it contains. If the survey or the site plan changes after we have begun, the change may affect the design, the schedule, and the fee, and we will advise you of the effect before we act on it.
Fee and Start of Work

Our fee for the work described above is a fixed sum of {{fact:f:E-2004-001.fee}}. The fee covers the design, the plan set, the supporting calculations, and the single round of response to the reviewing agency noted above. We will begin the work on {{fact:f:E-2004-001.start}}. Services beyond this scope, including additional review cycles, redesign to accommodate a change in the site plan, or attendance at hearings, will be undertaken only with your written authorization, and we will quote the additional cost before we proceed.
Invoicing and Payment

We will invoice monthly, in proportion to the work completed in the period. Each invoice is payable within thirty days of its date. Reimbursable expenses, including reproduction, agency fees, and delivery, are billed at cost and are in addition to the fee. Should an account remain unpaid sixty days after its date, we may, at our discretion, suspend work until the balance is brought current, and we will give you written notice before we do so. A suspension for non-payment extends our schedule by the length of the suspension.
Term and Termination

This agreement takes effect on the date work begins and continues until the plan set has been submitted and the reviewing agency's first round of comments has been answered. Either party may terminate the agreement on ten days' written notice to the other. On termination by you, you will pay for the services performed and the expenses incurred through the date of termination. The drawings, calculations, and files we prepare are our instruments of service and remain our property; on payment in full you are granted the use of them for this project.
Confidentiality

We will hold in confidence the site information, financial figures, and development plans you provide to us, and we will use them only to perform this work. We may disclose what a reviewing agency reasonably requires for its review, and what a court or a public body compels by law. This obligation survives the completion or termination of the work.
Limitation of Liability

We will perform this work with the care and skill ordinarily exercised by civil engineers practicing in this locality at this time. We make no other warranty, express or implied. Our total liability to {{fact:f:E-2004-001.client}} for any claim arising out of or related to this work, whether in contract or in tort, is limited to the amount of the fee paid under this agreement. We are not responsible for the means, methods, or safety of construction, nor for the acts or omissions of contractors or others not under our direct control.
Governing Law
This agreement is governed by the laws of the state in which the site is located. Any dispute arising under it that we cannot resolve between us will be submitted to the courts of that state.
Schedule

The work runs about five months from the start. We can hold that schedule so long as the survey and the site information reach us when they are needed and the reviewing agency responds within its usual time. Delay in either is outside our control. Should one threaten the completion of the work, we will tell you promptly and propose how to recover the time. We do not build float into the schedule for circumstances we cannot foresee, and we will not represent that we can.
Acceptance

If these terms meet with your approval, please sign both copies of this letter where indicated and return one copy to this office. On receipt, we will schedule the work to begin on the date stated above. Should any term require discussion, please telephone me and we will settle it before the work commences.
Sincerely,
To: The design and engineering team
From: Charles Olson
Re: Kickoff, Stormwater Management Plan for Johnson PLC

We are underway on the stormwater management plan for {{fact:f:E-2004-001.client}}, and I want us all working from the same picture. Our aim is a clean, buildable plan that clears the regional water authority's review on the first pass. Everything below serves that.

We started this engagement on {{fact:f:E-2004-001.start}}. David Dyer, the General Manager at Johnson PLC, is our contact for site information and for anything we need from the owner. Please bring owner questions to me, so we speak to him with one voice.

The design has to fit the development Johnson PLC has in mind, not a generic layout. So we will keep the owner's site plan in front of us and design to it. If the site plan shifts, I need to hear it early, because it moves our numbers and can move the schedule. Nothing we do downstream is safe if the base and the layout are not settled first.

A stormwater plan is only as good as the base it sits on. So our first effort goes to the survey and the drainage areas, and we will not model anything until we agree those are right. The rest of the work follows cleanly once the base is sound.
We have about five months, which is comfortable for a plan this size if we keep the base clean and avoid rework. The way to lose that time is to model early and redraw late. We will not do that.
How the work divides
Here is who carries what. It follows the way we usually split a plan like this.

items: Existing conditions and drainage areas: Charles Olson. I will set up the base sheet and pull the survey and topographic data into it.

Drainage design and detention: Pamela Warren. Pamela leads the hydrology and hydraulics, the detention sizing, and the water quality design, and she carries the coordination with the regional water authority.
Utility and stormwater drafting: Jeffrey Perez. Jeffrey takes the redlines and turns the sheets, checking his callouts against the design memoranda.
Erosion and sediment control: shared, with Pamela setting the approach and Jeffrey drafting the sheets.

blocks.text: Pamela owns the water authority relationship, so route review questions to her. She has taken plans through that review before, and she knows what they look for.
Where we begin
First we settle the base. I will circulate the existing-conditions sheet once the survey is in, and we will confirm the drainage areas together before anyone builds a model.

From there Pamela builds the model, and we hold a short design review before we commit to detention sizes. Jeffrey will hold the drafting until that review, so we are not redrawing sheets we could have drawn once.

Where it helps, Pamela will talk the approach through with the water authority's reviewers before we finalize it. A short conversation up front lets us fold their concerns into the design while it is still easy to change. That is how we clear the review on the first pass.

We are keeping the design memoranda current as we go, so Jeffrey always drafts from the latest direction and not from memory. Please write down any assumption you make and file it, so the next person sees it. Let us talk this Friday if any of this needs adjusting.
Stormwater Management Plan for Johnson PLC

blocks.text: Progress Meeting: Stormwater Management Plan for Johnson PLC

We met to review the drainage model and the preliminary detention design and to settle the open items with the owner. The design is on track and no change to scope came up. These minutes record what we covered and who owns each action.
Attendees

items: Pamela Warren, Project Engineer, Brackenridge Civil Group
Charles Olson, Design Technician, Brackenridge Civil Group
Jeffrey Perez, Design Technician, Brackenridge Civil Group
David Dyer, General Manager, Johnson PLC

blocks.text: Discussion

Charles Olson walked the existing-conditions sheet and the drainage areas. The areas check against the survey. One low point at the east property line drains off the site, and we agreed to carry that flow in the model rather than assume it away.

Charles Olson and Pamela Warren compared the drainage areas in the model against the base sheet, line for line. They agree. That check is worth the time it takes, because an area error early becomes a sizing error late.

Pamela Warren presented the preliminary runoff figures and the detention approach. The required release rates come from the regional water authority's standards, and the basin is sized to meet them. The water quality treatment will sit at the basin outlet. None of these numbers are final; they firm up once the grading is set.

Jeffrey Perez raised a conflict between the proposed storm line and an existing utility on the north side. We will shift the line and check the cover over it. David Dyer confirmed that the owner can furnish the record utility drawings this week, which tells us what is actually in the ground.

David Dyer noted that the owner's site plan is settled and will not change, which lets us fix the grading with confidence. That matters, because the detention sizing follows the grading. With the layout stable, we can move from preliminary numbers to a firm basin design.

We also went through the erosion and sediment control plan. It will follow the standard details: a stabilized construction entrance, silt fence along the down-gradient limits, and inlet protection. Jeffrey Perez will draft those sheets once the grading is far enough along to place them.

We talked about the outfall and the point where the basin discharges. The receiving channel can take the controlled flow, but the outlet needs riprap or an equivalent to hold against scour. Pamela Warren will set the outlet protection when she fixes the basin. Charles Olson will show the discharge point and the easement it sits in on the base sheet, so the drafting has it from the start.
We reviewed the schedule for {{fact:f:E-2004-001.client}}. We are near the midpoint and holding, and no additional work was requested.
Action Items

rows: Furnish record utility drawings for the north side
Revise the storm line to clear the existing utility and confirm cover
Confirm the drainage areas on the base sheet
Firm up detention sizing once grading is set

blocks.text: We closed by confirming the split of work for the next few weeks. Pamela Warren carries the detention design, Jeffrey Perez turns the utility and storm sheets, and Charles Olson keeps the base current. Nothing is waiting on a decision from the owner except the utility records.
Next step: Charles Olson closes the drainage areas so Pamela Warren can lock the model. We meet again at the next progress review.
Progress Report: Stormwater Management Plan

We are at the midpoint of the stormwater management plan for Johnson PLC, and the work is on schedule and within budget. This report sets out where the plan stands, what we completed since we began, what the second half holds, and the few items worth keeping an eye on. Nothing here calls for a decision from you today; it is a picture of steady progress.
Where we stand

The plan for {{fact:f:E-2004-001.client}} is roughly half complete. The existing conditions are set, the drainage areas are confirmed against the survey, and the hydrologic and hydraulic model is built and running. We have moved out of analysis and into the design of the detention and water quality facilities.

The work is tracking with our costs. We remain within the fixed fee of {{fact:f:E-2004-001.fee}} for the engagement, and we see nothing in the second half that would change that. No additional scope has been requested, and the design has not grown beyond what we agreed to prepare.

We are also keeping the reviewing agency in mind as we design, not only at submission. Pamela Warren has taken plans through this authority before, and she is shaping the detention and water quality design to what it expects. That is the surest way to clear the first round of comments without a redesign.
What we finished this period

Charles Olson set the existing-conditions base and reconciled the drainage areas against the survey. One low point at the property line drains off the site, and we chose to carry that flow in the model rather than assume it away. That keeps the design honest and avoids a surprise in review.

Pamela Warren built the model and produced the preliminary runoff figures. The required release rates follow the regional water authority's standards, and the detention basin is sized to meet them. The water quality measure will sit at the basin outlet, where it does the most good with the least added structure.

Jeffrey Perez found a conflict between a proposed storm line and an existing utility, and he has resolved it and is turning the affected sheets. We have asked the owner for the record utility drawings so we can confirm what is actually in the ground before we commit the line.

Across the period the three of us worked from the same design memoranda, so the sheets, the model, and the base all tell one story. Small as that sounds, it is what keeps a plan set clean under a careful review.

We also looked ahead to the outfall, where the basin discharges. The receiving channel can take the controlled flow, and we will protect the outlet against scour. Settling that now keeps it from becoming a comment later, when it is harder to fix.
What comes next
In the second half we complete the detention and water quality design and set the final grading. Pamela Warren will lock the model once the grading is fixed, since the two depend on each other.

Jeffrey Perez will draft the plan set from the completed design, and Charles Olson will keep the base sheet current as the design settles. We will bring the design to you for a review before anything is finalized.
We would like to hold that design review in the coming weeks, once the grading is set. We will propose a time that suits you and walk the plan with you in person.

After that review we assemble the plan set and the supporting calculations, and we prepare the submission to the regional water authority. Our fee covers one round of response to the agency's comments, and we have held time for it.

None of the second half depends on new information from you beyond the utility records already requested. That is the position we wanted to be in at the midpoint. It means the schedule is in our hands, and we intend to keep it there.
Items to watch

Two items could affect the schedule, and neither is serious today. The first is the record utility information. Until we have it, the storm line design carries an assumption we would prefer to confirm before we build on it.

The second is the grading. The detention sizing depends on it, so a late change to the grading would ripple into the basin design. We are holding the drafting until the grading is set, which keeps that risk small and avoids redrawing sheets.
In summary
We are at the midpoint, on schedule, and within the fee. The path to a submittable plan is clear, and the open items are ordinary ones we can close.
We will bring the design to you at the review before it is finalized. Prepared by Charles Olson, Design Technician.
